analysis: The supplied units are head-side excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md. The only changed line is 1846, a documentation row about `stop` handling. Neither supplied unit (lines 806-1611) contains that row, so I did not see the changed text directly; I relied on the patch excerpt. It says GPT-OSS sets `stopStringScope` to the Harmony `final` message, so analysis and tool-call frames never match a stop string, and the reported sequence replays the same scope. That is a documentation-only change. It touches no code, keys, endpoints, attestation, authorization, encryption or cache storage, so I found no regression against TB-002, TB-007, T-041, T-008 or the other threat entries. The examined surrounding text covers GLM serving, deadline admission, calibration and prompt-cache behavior. These sections describe existing behavior and are unchanged by this PR. Their prefix-cache statements (media excluded from prefix lookup, cache scope never crossed) are consistent with T-041's posture. I found no weakening of the TTL, scope, HMAC or kill-switch claims. Remaining questions for integration: the referenced code change (`StopHoldback`, `ModelEOSPolicy.stopStringScope`, `EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift`) is not in this batch. If it ships in the same PR, reviewers should confirm the scoped stop matching cannot leak hidden analysis or tool-call text through the reported stop sequence, and that streaming holdback does not emit content that belongs to a withheld channel. That is a code-level question about unseen files, not a finding on this doc change.
